'''Jerami Grant'''<ref>http://cuse.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=10332</ref> (born March 12, 1994) is an American [[basketball]] player who recently completed his college career for the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange]]. His father, [[Harvey Grant]], played college basketball at Clemson and Oklahoma and in the NBA with Washington (Bullets and Wizards), Portland and Philadelphia. Harvey was the 12th pick overall in the 1988 NBA Draft and played in the NBA for 11 years. 

Jerami has two older brothers: Jerai played college basketball at Clemson and Jerian is currently playing college basketball at Notre Dame. Jerian has started 33 of Notre Dame's 34 games so far in the 2012–13 season.

Jerami's uncle is [[Horace Grant]], who played college basketball at Clemson and was a four-time NBA champion with Chicago and Los Angeles. Horace was the 10th overall pick in 1987 by the Chicago Bulls and played in the NBA for 17 years.

==High school career==
Grant began playing on the varsity basketball team at DeMatha Catholic when he was a [[Tenth grade|sophomore]]. Coming out of high school he was the 11th ranked power forward in the country according to the ESPN 100 rankings.<ref>https://www.suathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=9477&path=mbasket</ref>

==College career==

===College statistics===

Grant's minutes increased steadily in his first season at Syracuse. He averaged 11 minutes per game in the first 10 games of the season, then 18 minutes per game in the next 10 games, up 61%. He had more minutes per game in Syracuse's last four games in January 2013 than the other three players in the rotation in the back of Syracuse's 2-3 zone defense ([[Rakeem Christmas]], [[DaJuan Coleman]] and [[Baye Moussa Keita]]). He had his first start of his college basketball career in February 2013 after DaJuan Coleman injured his knee.
